metadata.title: Druckenmiller loads up on Amazon and AMD while dumping some chipmakers, 13F shows

content.text:
Investing.com -- Stanley Druckenmiller's Duquesne Family Office executed a dramatic reshuffling of its portfolio during the latest quarter, highlighted by a massive rotation back into mega-cap technology and a decisive exit from several legacy semiconductor names. Most notably, the firm increased its core equity position in Amazon.com Inc (NASDAQ:AMZN) by more than 1,000% to 541,600 shares, while simultaneously more than doubling its call options on the e-commerce giant.
Against that backdrop, Druckenmiller aggressively reconfigured his exposure to the semiconductor and artificial intelligence landscape. Duquesne entirely liquidated its stakes in Broadcom Inc (NASDAQ:AVGO), Intel Corporation (NASDAQ:INTC), and Micron Technology Inc (NASDAQ:MU), opting instead to initiate a new 72,900-share position in Advanced Micro Devices Inc (NASDAQ:AMD) while slightly lifting its existing holdings in Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (NYSE:TSM). The portfolio transformation also reflected a renewed appetite for broader market leadership and strategic media assets. The firm established a significant new position in Alphabet Inc Class A (NASDAQ:GOOGL) with 336,300 shares, bolstered its technology outlook with new call options on Meta Platforms Inc (NASDAQ:META) and Tesla Inc (NASDAQ:TSLA), and initiated a robust 2.8 million-share stake in Fox Corp across two share classes.
Meanwhile, the latest regulatory filings indicate growing conviction in the trajectory of the commercial aviation sector. Duquesne initiated a sizable new position of 603,000 shares in Delta Air Lines Inc (NYSE:DAL), while in turn nearly tripling its existing stake in United Airlines Holdings Inc (NASDAQ:UAL) to roughly 795,000 shares.
In a strategic pivot toward AI infrastructure, the family office expanded its operational focus into the data center space. The firm established positions in several key operators, most notably acquiring more than 4 million shares of Bitdeer Technologies Group (NASDAQ:BTDR) alongside a new 754,800-share stake in Riot Platforms (NASDAQ:RIOT).
By contrast, Druckenmiller moved swiftly to trim or exit several positions. Beyond the high-profile semiconductor exits, Duquesne completely liquidated its holdings in Cloudflare Inc (NYSE:NET) and MercadoLibre Inc (NASDAQ:MELI), while drastically narrowing its exposure to Alcoa Corp (NYSE:AA) and Arm Holdings ADR (NASDAQ:ARM) by more than 70% each.
